title: Organizational AI adoption readiness - interview instrument
content_notice: DRAFT INSTRUMENT CONTENT. These prompts are a starting point for operational interviews. Nothing here is a University finding or a measured University figure.
recording_rule: Responses are recorded at TEAM granularity with a contributor COUNT only. No individual identity is collected, stored, or attributed. This instrument assesses organizational capability and must never be used to rate a person.

dimensions.label: AI literacy
dimensions.intent: Whether the team shares a written, consultable understanding of where these tools belong and where they do not.

indicators.prompt: Where has the team written down what these tools are used for here, and what they are not used for?
indicators.artifact_request: The written statement or guidance page, with the date it was last reviewed.
indicators.why_it_matters: A shared written boundary is what lets two people on the same team answer a borderline request the same way.

indicators.prompt: When someone is unsure whether a task is appropriate for an assistant, what do they consult before deciding?
indicators.artifact_request: The page, checklist, or thread they name.
indicators.why_it_matters: Distinguishes a consultable resource from an individual habit that leaves with the person.

indicators.prompt: How does the team describe what these tools get wrong on the work you actually do?
indicators.artifact_request: Any written note of known failure modes for the tasks currently in use.
indicators.why_it_matters: Naming specific failure modes is the difference between literacy and enthusiasm.

dimensions.label: Practical training
dimensions.intent: Whether capability was built on the team's own recurring work, and whether it survives staff turnover.

indicators.prompt: What hands-on practice has the team had on its own recurring tasks, as opposed to a general awareness session?
indicators.artifact_request: Training record or session notes naming the tasks practised.
indicators.why_it_matters: General awareness rarely transfers to the team's actual queue.

indicators.prompt: How does someone joining the team learn the assisted parts of the workflow?
indicators.artifact_request: Onboarding material that covers the assisted step.
indicators.why_it_matters: Capability that exists only in the current staff is a dependency, not a capability.

dimensions.label: Workflow fit
dimensions.intent: Whether assistance is placed at identified points in real procedures, including where it was deliberately removed.

indicators.prompt: Which recurring workflows currently include an assisted step, and at which point in the procedure?
indicators.artifact_request: The procedure document showing the step.
indicators.why_it_matters: Placement in a written procedure is what makes the practice repeatable by someone else.

indicators.prompt: Where was an assisted step tried and then narrowed or removed?
indicators.artifact_request: The change note, ticket, or decision record.
indicators.why_it_matters: A recorded retreat is strong evidence of real evaluation; its absence can mean nothing was ever checked.

indicators.prompt: Which steps are explicitly excluded from assistance, and on what basis?
indicators.artifact_request: The written exclusion and its stated reason.
indicators.why_it_matters: Exclusions show the boundary is operational rather than aspirational.

dimensions.label: Available support
dimensions.intent: Whether there is a reachable, non-singular place to take a problem with an assisted workflow.

indicators.prompt: Who does the team ask when an assisted workflow behaves unexpectedly?
indicators.artifact_request: The named contact, queue, or routing rule.
indicators.why_it_matters: Separates a support path from an informally helpful colleague.

indicators.prompt: What happens to that question when the usual contact is unavailable?
indicators.artifact_request: The escalation path, if it is written down.
indicators.why_it_matters: Single-person support is the most common hidden dependency in this area.

dimensions.label: Knowledge sharing
dimensions.intent: Whether something one person learns becomes reusable by the team, and whether it is kept correct.

indicators.prompt: Where does a useful approach that one person worked out get recorded so others can use it?
indicators.artifact_request: The register, page, or channel, with its actual entries.
indicators.why_it_matters: Sharing that happens only in conversation does not survive a staffing change.

indicators.prompt: How is that shared material reviewed or corrected when it stops being right?
indicators.artifact_request: Review or last-checked dates on entries.
indicators.why_it_matters: An unreviewed register becomes a source of confidently wrong practice.

dimensions.label: Capacity to evaluate new approaches
dimensions.intent: Whether the team can tell a genuinely better result from a faster-looking one, and can reverse a decision.

indicators.prompt: Describe the last new approach the team trialled and how it decided whether to keep it.
indicators.artifact_request: The evaluation note or decision record.
indicators.why_it_matters: Trialling without a recorded decision leaves the team unable to explain why it works the way it does.

indicators.prompt: What would the team check to distinguish a genuinely better result from one that merely arrives faster?
indicators.artifact_request: The acceptance check or known-answer set, if any exists.
indicators.why_it_matters: Without an acceptance check, speed is the only thing anyone can actually observe.

indicators.prompt: Who can stop an approach the team has already adopted, and on what evidence?
indicators.artifact_request: The written decision owner or reversal criterion.
indicators.why_it_matters: An adoption nobody can reverse is a commitment, not an evaluation.
